spec.description: How the system tunes, heals, and learns itself — fleet-wide and per-device (merged from the former Autonomous Behavior + Transparency dashboards).

spec.title: 🤖 What is this dashboard?
spec.description: Section header.

options.content:
**Is the system actually getting smarter, and can I trust what it does while I'm not watching?**

This dashboard is Prometheus-only by design -- every panel here works even if Loki is never wired up (see System Health's own note on that). It covers four things the other dashboards don't: which reasoning path resolved each decision and whether that mix is improving over time, how much self-healing is autonomous vs a human tap, whether the autotune self-calibration system is adjusting itself safely, and whether every scheduled background job actually ran when it was supposed to.

spec.title: 🧭 Brain 1 / HEE: Decision-Path Mix Over Time
spec.description: Which branch of decision_engine.py's decision order actually resolved each evaluation (hard_stop/tier5_confirmed/hypothesis_high/hypothesis_suspicious/tier4_unconfirmed/ml_anomaly/benign). This is the direct 'is the system getting smarter over time' signal: watch the hard_stop/tier5 share shrink and the benign share grow across weeks as autotune calibration, CL-AFPE's trust cache, and the CDN/vendor allowlist absorb more of what used to need a hard corroborated signal to resolve correctly.

spec.title: 🧭 Decision-Path Share (Last 24h)
spec.description: Same data as the timeseries to the left, collapsed to one 24h window -- the proportions are the headline number; use the timeseries to spot exactly when the mix shifted.

spec.title: 🛡️ Self-Healing: Domains Immunized by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_domains_immunized_total split by source (autonomous = CL-AFPE's own Stage 2/3 suppress path, operator = a Telegram 'Mark False Positive' tap, llm_validated = Ollama's autonomous 4-hourly validation pass). The whole point of this session's self-calibration work was to make 'autonomous' and 'llm_validated' the dominant sources over time, not 'operator' -- a human shouldn't need to keep pace with every alert for the system to keep healing itself.

spec.title: 🛡️ Self-Healing: Sensitivity Adjustments by Source
spec.description: fp_engine_sigma_shifts_total split the same way -- every TUNE_DOWN (a confirmed false positive widening a device's baseline) or TUNE_UP (a confirmed threat tightening it) event, attributed to what triggered it.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Global Suppress Threshold — Effective vs Baseline
spec.description: The single most direct 'is the system healing itself' chart: the live effective fp_combined_suppress_threshold (green, from state/config_overrides.json if calibration has acted, else identical to baseline) against your own hand-set config.yaml baseline (the two lines start identical; effective should trend at or below baseline over time, never above -- calibration is one-directional by design and never raises it).

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Calibration Pass Outcomes (Cumulative)
spec.description: Every calibration pass classified by outcome: applied (threshold actually lowered), refused_ambiguous (an uncorrected UNCERTAIN alert overlapped the confirmed-FP range -- refused to auto-resolve that), insufficient_samples (not enough pooled corrections yet), no_change_needed (evidence didn't support going any lower than the current value). Refusals are as informative as applications here -- they're proof the system isn't blindly loosening just because it can.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Per-Device Calibrated Thresholds
spec.description: Devices that have earned their own calibrated suppress threshold (>=3 pooled corrections of that specific device's own evidence) -- devices not listed here still use the global effective value. A strongly different profile (e.g. a chatty IoT device) converges on its own number here rather than forcing one global threshold onto every device.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Evidence Samples Pooled (Global)
spec.description: How close the global pass is to its next calibration decision: corrected = confirmed false positives pooled since the last write (needs >=5 to act), uncorrected = never-corrected UNCERTAIN alerts in the same window (any overlap with the corrected range blocks calibration entirely, regardless of count).

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Time Since Last Successful Run
spec.description: Scheduled every 4 hours by scripts/scheduler.py. Should never exceed roughly 4-5h under normal operation -- a much larger number here means the job silently stopped firing (exactly the class of bug a job-key/filename mismatch caused once already in this project) without anyone noticing until they went looking.

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Calls / Cache Hits / Deferred (Last Run)
spec.description: A single noisy pattern that fired 50 times only ever costs one Ollama call, reused from the 7-day cache on every subsequent run it keeps recurring -- this is the direct evidence that 'call Ollama sparingly' is actually happening, not just a log claim. Deferred > 0 means the per-run cap was hit; those patterns retry next run, prioritized by which repeated most.

spec.title: 🕵️ Ollama: Cumulative Validated Verdicts
spec.description: Every LLM classification that passed DeterministicValidator's hallucination guardrail, since state/ollama_run_stats.json existed, split benign vs malicious. This is a running total, not a per-run count -- the trend across weeks is what matters.

spec.title: 🔓 Pi-hole Unblocks by Reason
spec.description: 'immunized' = an autonomous or operator correction released a block that was no longer warranted (the core of 'block only what's absolutely necessary'). 'manual' = an explicit operator release via the Grafana IPC endpoint or a device-level release. This is the release-side counterpart to the block-side 'Lifetime Threats Blocked' panel on the Main Overview dashboard -- until this session neither existed.

spec.title: 🔓 Router Isolation Releases by Reason
spec.description: 'device_marked_safe' = automatic release once a device is confirmed safe (safe_ips/patterns). 'manual' = an explicit operator release via Telegram or Grafana. Router isolation is deliberately latched -- it is never auto-released purely because traffic decayed to zero -- so every release here is a real, attributable decision, not a timeout.

spec.title: 📅 Scheduled-Job Health
spec.description: Time since each scheduled job's last successful completion, and how long that run took. Directly targets the exact class of bug already found once in this project -- a job-key/filename mismatch that silently never ran, with nothing surfacing the failure beyond a daemon log line nobody was watching. Expected staleness: ollama_soc ~4h, retro_hunter/top_domains_report/train_fp_classifier ~24h.

spec.title: 📅 Retro-Hunt Findings (Cumulative)
spec.description: Total retroactive threat-intel matches found by retro_hunter.py since state/job_health.json existed -- domains your network talked to that were unknown-clean at the time but have since been classified malicious by fresh OSINT.

spec.title: 📡 Reactive Capture (Fritzbox WiFi Bursts) — full transparency
spec.description: Section header.

options.content:
**Before this: Zeek had zero real network-flow visibility into any WiFi device** -- only the two wired devices got lateral-movement, JA3/JA4, and DNS-evasion detection. Reactive capture fixes this without running WiFi capture 24/7 (which costs ~3GB/hour): short (~2 min) triggered bursts on the Fritzbox's own radios, reprocessed through the SAME real Zeek policy the wired taps use, so a WiFi device that had traffic during a burst gets real signal for the first time -- no separate, less-tested detection path.

The panels below answer the honest operational question: **is this actually running, and is it actually working?** Bursts are capped to a shared hourly budget and only one can physically run at a time (the radio is a single shared resource) -- 'deferred' below means a trigger fired but had to wait, not that it was lost.

spec.title: Bursts Dispatched (Total)
spec.description: Cumulative reactive-capture bursts that actually ran (passed the hourly budget AND found no other burst already in flight).

spec.title: Bursts Deferred (Total)
spec.description: Triggers that fired but had to wait -- either the shared hourly budget (reactive_capture_max_bursts_per_hour) was exhausted, or a different burst was already using the radio. Deferred triggers are reconsidered later, not dropped.

spec.title: Time Since Last Successful Burst
spec.description: How long since a reactive-capture burst last completed. A large number here on an active network means triggers have stopped firing or completing -- worth checking the service log.

spec.title: Burst Outcomes Over Time (dispatched vs deferred)
spec.description: dispatched = a real capture ran. deferred = hourly budget exhausted. deferred_concurrent = a different burst already had the radio (BUGFIX this session -- concurrent bursts were corrupting each other's output; now serialized).

spec.title: Reactive-Capture Errors by Stage (Cumulative Rate)
spec.description: Where in the pipeline a burst failed: capture (router/auth), conversion (AVM->standard pcap), zeek_reprocess (BUGFIX this session -- was 100% failing due to a relative-path bug, now fixed), or dns_evasion_audit. Should trend toward zero.

spec.title: Data Captured per Radio (Cumulative Bytes)
spec.description: Raw AVM pcap bytes captured per radio across all bursts -- sanity-check against expected burst size (burst_seconds x typical throughput) if this looks unexpectedly flat or huge.

spec.title: DNS-Evasion Findings (Cumulative)
spec.description: Total dns_evasion_anomaly findings across every device from every burst -- a real connection during a burst window with no DNS explanation and no recognized-safe (CDN/VPN) infrastructure match. See the section below for per-device detail.

spec.title: Stale Files Auto-Cleaned (Cumulative)
spec.description: Orphaned capture files removed by the periodic disk-safety sweep -- catches files left behind if the process crashed mid-burst. Should stay near zero under normal operation (the per-burst cleanup handles the normal path); a rising count means bursts are crashing, not just erroring.

spec.title: 🌐 Local Confirmed-Intel Store — the network's shared memory
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: **The actual 'getting smarter over time' mechanic.** Once ANY device on this network is confirmed connecting to a malicious IP/domain (a Stage-1 hard-stop, or a genuinely corroborated HIGH/CRITICAL decision), that IOC is remembered here. The next time a **different** device connects to the same IOC, it hard-stops immediately instead of re-earning two independent evidence sources from scratch -- the network gets collectively harder to compromise via the same infrastructure the longer it runs. Entries expire (`local_confirmed_intel_ttl_seconds`, config.yaml) since infrastructure months-old may be repurposed or abandoned.

spec.title: Confirmed Malicious IPs Tracked
spec.description: Current non-expired IP entries in the local confirmed-threat store.

spec.title: Confirmed Malicious Domains Tracked
spec.description: Current non-expired domain entries in the local confirmed-threat store.

spec.title: Cross-Device Hard-Stops (network-effect saves)
spec.description: Stage-1 hard-stops fired because a DIFFERENT device had already confirmed this exact IOC -- the direct payoff of the store above. Each of these is a threat caught immediately instead of needing to independently re-earn a HIGH/CRITICAL bar.

spec.title: Local Confirmed-Intel Store Growth Over Time
spec.description: The store's size, by kind, over time -- should generally trend up (more confirmed threats known) with occasional drops as TTL-expired entries are pruned. A store that never grows means confirmed threats aren't reaching Stage 1, worth cross-checking against System Health's 'Confirmed Threats' panel.

spec.title: 🕸️ New Detectors: ARP-Sweep & DNS-Evasion (Per-Device)
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: Two detectors added this session, both feeding the LightGBM classifier's 11-dimension feature vector. **ARP-sweep**: a device probing many distinct local IPs in a short window (host-discovery / LAN reconnaissance) -- corroborating evidence, not an automatic hard-stop, since some IoT discovery protocols look similar. **DNS-evasion ratio**: from a reactive-capture burst, the fraction of a device's real connections that have NO explaining DNS query and NO recognized-safe (CDN/VPN) destination -- the signature of something bypassing DNS-based detection entirely.

spec.title: Per-Device ARP-Sweep Count & DNS-Evasion Ratio
spec.description: Live values as currently tracked by the pipeline. arp_sweep = distinct hosts ARP-requested in the current window. dns_evasion_ratio = most recent reactive-capture blind-spot-audit result, 0.0-1.0 (0 = every connection during the last burst was explained).

spec.title: ARP-Sweep Threshold Calibration Outcomes (Cumulative)
spec.description: Autotune's calibration pass results for the per-device arp_sweep_unique_targets_threshold: applied (tightened/loosened this device's threshold), no_change_needed, or insufficient_samples. Mirrors the same self-calibration pattern already proven for the global suppress threshold above.

spec.title: ARP-Sweep Evidence Pool (corrected vs confirmed)
spec.description: Per-device correction/confirmation counts feeding the calibration pass above -- 'confirmed' growing faster than 'corrected' for a device is autotune's signal that this detector has earned more sensitivity there, not less.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: ARP-Sweep Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: PHASE 30 (metrics-audit gap fix): home_ids_autotune_arp_sweep_threshold_effective already had sibling calibration-outcome and evidence-pool panels below, but its own current value was never plotted anywhere. Devices listed here have their OWN calibrated arp_sweep_unique_targets_threshold (from either the reactive correction path or train_fp_classifier.py's weekly bidirectional pass) -- devices not listed still use the global config.yaml default.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Connection-Abuse Unique-IP Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: PHASE 30: home_ids_autotune_conn_abuse_threshold_effective -- threat_signals.py's zeek_conn_abuse check (s0_rej_unique > threshold) uses this per device instead of the global conn_abuse_unique_ip_threshold default once a CONNECTION_ABUSE alert citing zeek_conn_abuse/s0_rej evidence has been corrected for that device. Devices not listed here still use the global default.

spec.title: ⚙️ Autotune: Long-Connection Duration Threshold — Effective (Per-Device)
spec.description: PHASE 30: home_ids_autotune_long_conn_threshold_effective -- threat_signals.py's zeek_long_conn check (max_duration > threshold) uses this per device instead of the global long_conn_duration_threshold default once a CONNECTION_ABUSE alert citing zeek_long_conn evidence has been corrected for that device. Devices not listed here still use the global default.

spec.title: 🧭 Persistence-Escalated Alerts by Signature
spec.description: home_ids_persistence_escalation_total -- alerts whose confidence/state was escalated purely because the SAME uncorroborated signal kept recurring (decision['escalated_via_persistence']), not because of new independent evidence. Deliberately capped below every genuinely-corroborated HIGH and excluded from authorizing IPS containment on its own. A signature dominating this chart is a candidate for its own detector-specific threshold, the same way arp_sweep/conn_abuse/long_conn evolved from generic thresholds into per-device learned ones.

spec.title: 🧠 Per-Device Self-Learning
spec.description: Everything above this line is a fleet-wide aggregate. Everything below (and every panel already patched above) respects the $device picker at the top of this dashboard -- pick one device to see just its own tuning history.

spec.title: ⚙️ Device-Profile Corrections by Threshold Key & Source
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_device_profile_correction_total -- cumulative reactive/calibration corrections applied to a device's learned-threshold profile, by which threshold key was touched and who/what made the correction. Filterable by $device now that the metric carries a hostname label (fixed this session).

spec.title: 🧪 CL-AFPE 3-Stage Funnel (Evaluated → Hard-Stopped → Suppressed)
spec.description: How many alerts CL-AFPE evaluated, how many were confirmed threats (hard-stop bypass, never eligible for suppression), and how many were actually suppressed as false positives.

spec.title: Zeek Network Monitor
spec.description: home_ids_zeek_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel.

spec.title: Pi-hole IPS
spec.description: home_ids_ips_pihole_status -- reference copy of the Overview dashboard's identical panel.

spec.title: 🦈 Suricata Binary Health (Boot-Time)
spec.description: PHASE 30: home_ids_suricata_binary_health -- the one-shot --build-info smoke test result from main.py's boot sequence. No data = reactive_capture_suricata_enabled is false. See the next panel for the live scan success rate.

spec.title: 🌱 Self-Healing & Self-Learning Events (Fleet-Wide)
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: **Everything below is new this session.** These are the mechanisms that previously only produced a log line (or nothing at all) -- transfer learning, retroactive identity merges, re-identification, baseline/probation lifecycle transitions, device-type reclassification, and the per-device ML model's own warmup/retrain/anti-poisoning/invalidation cycle. Panels here are fleet-wide aggregates; where the underlying metric carries a hostname label, the $device picker above narrows it to one device (see also Device Deep Dive's own per-device copy of these).

spec.title: 🌱 Transfer-Learning Seeds by Device Type
spec.description: home_ids_transfer_learning_seeds_total -- fires once per NEW device, when its starting hourly baselines are seeded from peer devices of the same device_type instead of cold-starting from zero (state_guard.py's get_or_create()).

spec.title: 🔗 Identity Self-Healing: Merges & Re-Identifications
spec.description: Three related but distinct identity events: identity_merges (a fragmented orphan device_id folded into its richer canonical identity -- this session's core fix), reidentify_migrations (a device kept its identity across a MAC rotation via DHCP/JA4 fingerprint match), reidentify_ambiguous (a re-identify candidate too weak to auto-merge, triggers a reactive capture to try to resolve it).

spec.title: Lifetime Identity Merges
spec.description: Cumulative home_ids_identity_merges_total since the service last restarted.

spec.title: Lifetime Re-ID Migrations
spec.description: Cumulative home_ids_identity_reidentify_migrations_total since the service last restarted.

spec.title: Lifetime Re-ID Ambiguous
spec.description: Cumulative home_ids_identity_reidentify_ambiguous_total since the service last restarted.

spec.title: Lifetime Profile Discards
spec.description: Cumulative home_ids_device_profile_discards_total (merge + prune reasons combined) since the service last restarted.

spec.title: Device-Profile Discards by Reason
spec.description: home_ids_device_profile_discards_total -- an FP-calibration profile or ML model being discarded, split by why: "merge" (folded into a canonical identity, orphan's own history dropped) vs "prune" (device aged out of tracking entirely).

spec.title: Baseline Poisoning Transitions
spec.description: home_ids_baseline_poisoning_transitions_total -- "entered": a device's risk score crossed the poisoning threshold and its baseline ingestion froze. "recovered": it dropped back below it. A device flapping between the two rapidly is itself worth investigating.

spec.title: Probation Transitions
spec.description: home_ids_probation_transitions_total -- "entered": a new or reset device dropped below the sample-count floor and re-entered probation. "graduated": it crossed back above it and is now scored normally.

spec.title: Per-Device ML Model Lifecycle (Fleet-Wide)
spec.description: The per-device IsolationForest anomaly model's own self-adaptation, summed across all devices: warmup_completions (first fit after enough samples), retrain_events (periodic refit), poisoning_rejections (training samples skipped during the post-confirmed-threat anti-poisoning window), model_invalidations (a stale/incompatible model discarded and reset after a feature-shape mismatch).

spec.title: Device-Type Reclassifications
spec.description: home_ids_device_type_reclassifications_total -- a device's inferred type actually changed (e.g. the cold-start 'laptop' fallback replaced once a real hostname resolved -- this session's apply_device_type() fix). A stable hostname re-infers to the same type every cycle, so this only fires on genuine changes, not noise.

spec.title: Behavioral-Familiarity Fingerprint Growth (Per-Device)
spec.description: home_ids_baseline_familiarity_entries_total -- size of each device's learned port/ASN/domain 'known-normal' fingerprint (VERSION 11 per-device baseline). A device whose line keeps climbing is still actively building up what's normal for it; a flat line means it's settled. Filterable by the $device picker above.

spec.title: Retro-Hunt Findings by Device
spec.description: home_ids_retro_hunt_findings_by_device -- per-device breakdown of retro_hunter.py's local-intel cross-reference matches (a device's OWN past connection now matches an IOC a DIFFERENT device has since confirmed). Scoped to that specific match type only -- the external-ThreatIntel historical-domain re-scan (the other half of home_ids_retro_hunt_findings_total) has no per-device attribution by construction, see retro_hunter.py's _count_findings_by_device() docstring.
Caption for the subsystem status tiles below.

options.content: 🟢/ONLINE/ARMED = working right now. 🔴/OFFLINE/UNAVAILABLE = that specific layer is down -- the other containment layers keep working independently, hover any tile for exactly what to check.
